# Visibility and Geometry

> **Draft chapter map.** Explain how the renderer decides what geometry to prepare and draw, across meshes, volumes, and changing levels of detail.

## Visibility Is a Budget Decision

- Establish that rendering every object is not a viable definition of correctness.
- Connect visibility to view-dependent relevance and finite frame budgets.

### Frustum, Occlusion, and Distance

- Explain broad classes of culling without treating one technique as universally required.
- Compare CPU and GPU responsibility based on data size and latency.

#### Conservative Results and Temporal Feedback

- Discuss false positives, delayed results, and stability trade-offs.
- Connect visibility feedback to the advisory-feedback contract.

## Geometry as an Extensible Family

- Explain why an engine should not make a single primitive representation its universal object model.
- Introduce meshes, instancing, terrain, and volumes as renderer-facing realizations of game intent.

### Mesh Streams and Levels of Detail

- Cover shared geometry, instances, LOD selection, and transition quality.
- Relate streaming demand to geometric detail.

#### Voxel Volumes as First-Class Geometry

- Use Smallworld to illustrate a hybrid voxel-mesh renderer.
- Explain what is generalizable and what is specific to the engine’s target worlds.

## Opaque Geometry Produces Shared Evidence

- Explain why a depth pre-pass and an opaque geometry/GBuffer pass are more than draw stages: they create the depth, material, normal, emissive, and motion information consumed by later work.
- Compare deferred, forward, and hybrid paths in terms of light count, material freedom, memory bandwidth, and the needs of opaque versus transparent geometry.

### GBuffer, Motion, and Identification

- Describe the purpose of material attributes, encoded normals, depth, and per-pixel velocity; connect velocity to temporal anti-aliasing, temporal upscaling, and motion blur.
- Cover picking and debug identification as deliberate, on-demand services rather than a permanent full-resolution ID target that taxes every frame.

#### Decals and Surface Modification

- Place projected deferred decals after opaque geometry and before lighting, showing how they amend existing surface data without creating a separate object model.
- Explain receiving flags, normal blending, ordering, and why decals belong to the shared render contract rather than a game-specific shortcut.

## Deformation and Animation at the Boundary

- Explain the handoff from animation data to renderable geometry.
- Set up later detail on compute skinning and deformation passes.

### Verification and Profiling

- Define useful counters for visibility, draw work, and geometry throughput.
- Connect tuning decisions to instrumentation and visual correctness.

#### Common Failure Modes

- Cover popping, unstable LOD, over-culling, and unbounded draw preparation.
- Tie remedies to explicit quality and latency policy.
